newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour to veto majority vote on Social Chapter.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour to veto majority vote on Social Chapter.

text.p: A UK Labour government would sign up to the European Union Social Chapter but would oppose any extension to majority voting on social issues, opposition finance spokesman Gordon Brown said on Monday.

"I can assure you that not only do we have no plans to extend qualified majority voting in these areas under the Social Chapter, but that we will veto any attempt to do so," he told top industry leaders at the Confederation of British Industry's annual conference.

"Because we believe that in this important area an empty chair is not in Britain's interests, we will sign the Social Chapter....but we will not allow qualified majority voting to be extended to those areas it should not be," he said.
The Social Chapter guarantees minimum rights for workers.
A survey released on the eve of the CBI's conference showed 73 percent of nearly 1,700 firms polled wanted the government to retain its opt-out from the Chapter.
CBI delegates fear that signing up now could lead to Britain being saddled with more legislation and regulations in the future.

Brown said a minimum level of economic integration must be reached before Britain signs up for a single European currency. A Labour government would also need to be convinced the economic conditions were right for EMU to succeed.
"And we would need to ensure public support for any such step," he said.
"Labour must play a full part in any future discussions of European economic cooperation and monetary union and that means keeping Britain's options open," Brown added.
